  • Method Details

    • run

      void run()

      Runs the main-loop of the underlying thread, updating Queues mapped to signals that have been registered, and updating Queues from the current system timestamp. Additionally, synchronization operations should occur to ensure multi-threading safety through the use of signal locks.

      Should only be called once via start(), as the method contains an internal while-loop that continues as long as the Reporter is alive, and Closeable.close() has not yet been called.

      Specified by:
      run in interface Runnable

    • start

      void start()

      Makes a call to run() and begins updating values appropriately. Ideally, calls to this method are only made once, but the method should contain logic to prevent multiple calls to run() concurrently.

      However, this method should be capable of being used repeatedly with multiple calls to start and halt()

    • halt

      void halt(long Timeout)
      Waits for the provided amount of time and attempts to join this thread into the calling thread. Should provide logic to ensure that it can be used repeatedly in conjunction with start().
      Parameters:
      Timeout - Milliseconds to wait before joining the thread

    • halt

      default void halt()
      Waits for 'zero' milliseconds and attempts to join this thread into the calling thread. Should provide logic to ensure that it can be used repeatedly in conjunction with start().

    • register

      Queue<Provides> register(@NonNull Source Signal)
      Adds a signal to the collection of signals, these signals act as a source for associated numerical values which are provided back via a Queue, where the most recently provided element is the last element in the Queue.

      Note that this is done concurrently with updating timestamp() Queues, so each update-cycle of run() creates a pair of signal-values and timestamps that can be used to better interpolate values as opposed to a standard 20-millisecond cycle provided by Subsystem.periodic(), which provides lower accuracy.

      Parameters:
      Signal - Supplier of Numerical values which can be parsed as a double.
      Returns:
      Queue, should be retained and used to collect values periodically.
      See Also:
      • Figures.from(DoubleCircularBuffer)

    • timestamp

      Queue<Double> timestamp()
      Creates a new Queue of standard size, and adds it to the collection of timestamp Queues. Each timestamp Queue contains the timestamp from a timestamp of a run-cycle, where the last element in the Queue is the most recent timestamp.

      Note that this is done concurrently with updating timestamp Queues, so each update-cycle of run() creates a pair of signal-values and timestamps that can be used to better interpolate values as opposed to a standard 20-millisecond cycle provided by Subsystem.periodic(), which provides lower accuracy.

      Returns:
      Queue, should be retained and used to collect values periodically.
      See Also:
      • Figures.from(DoubleCircularBuffer)
